resources.string: Shapes the TLS handshake toward the edge so DPI has a harder time matching it. Off by default; each mode changes the bytes on the wire.

Split modes only apply to the HTTP/2 carrier. Turn on "MASQUE over HTTP/2" on the Connection page to use them; on HTTP/3 the ClientHello sits inside QUIC frames the engine does not split. The custom SNI below works on both.
Spoofing shapes a TLS ClientHello, which WireGuard and WARP×2 do not send. Pick a MASQUE transport on the Connection page to use it.

Presented to the MASQUE edge instead of the default name, on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3. The edge certificate is pinned, so a wrong name cannot open you to interception - but the edge may also refuse it. Leave empty for the default. Applies from the next connect.
